highlights: Implementation managers solved customer use cases in isolation — how a problem had been solved lived in people’s heads and scattered documents. Atlas makes that knowledge searchable. Built as a Lovable app with Claude agents and custom skills, using Supermemory to index product docs, internal docs, and approved solutions so the agent retrieves only what is relevant.

After a customer call or ticket, an agent reads the call transcript, Freshdesk tickets, Slack threads, and project documents, lists the use cases discussed, and records the solution agreed — or proposes one from Rocketlane’s product docs when none was. The implementation manager approves or revises each one, and approved solutions are saved to the knowledge base.

When someone asks how a use case was solved, Atlas finds the approved solution and checks it against live sources — Notion, Slack, the Rocketlane instance, and current API docs — before answering. If a feature has since been retired, it explains how it was done then and how to do it now.

Answers marked helpful are cached and returned for near-identical questions (95%+ match) without a new search. Answers marked wrong capture a reason; a validator agent classifies the failure, such as a data miss or a context miss, and queues it for an admin to fix the sources or the agent’s skills.
